message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure they receive a safe, habitable living environment. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes. This is not legal advice; if you have a specific dispute, consult a qualified attorney. | Category | Key Rights | What It Means | |----------|------------|---------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must return deposit within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear. | Landlords cannot keep deposits without proper documentation or exceed the statutory limit. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe condition. | If the landlord fails to repair, the tenant can withhold rent, repair and deduct, or terminate the lease. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are prohibited unless the lease explicitly allows them. | Landlords cannot impose arbitrary late fees; any fee must be in the lease. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for residential leases longer than one year.
• Landlord must provide a copy of the lease to the tenant. | Tenants can enforce written lease terms and refuse to sign if the lease is missing required disclosures. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenancy.
• For eviction: 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease violation. | Landlords must give proper notice before filing an eviction action. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenant has the right to use the premises without interference. | Landlords cannot enter without notice (except emergencies). | | **Entry Rules** | • Landlord must give at least 24‑hour written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | Landlords cannot repeatedly enter without notice. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | Fair Housing Act applies to all residential rentals. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent, but only if the lease allows it. | Tenants can take action if the landlord neglects repairs. | | **Termination of Lease** | • Tenant may terminate lease early if landlord breaches habitability or fails to provide required notices. | Tenants can move out without penalty if the landlord violates the lease. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Landlord may deduct for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, cleaning, and other costs specified in the lease. | Landlords must provide an itemized statement of deductions. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in district court and follow the statutory notice requirements. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas does not have statewide rent control; rent increases are governed by lease terms. | Landlords can raise rent according to lease or at lease renewal. | | **Subletting** | • Tenant may sublet only if the lease permits it or with landlord’s written consent. | Landlords cannot unreasonably deny subletting. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide water, electricity, gas, and heat. | Landlords cannot cut off utilities without proper notice. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to insure the property; tenant may obtain renter’s insurance. | Tenants can protect themselves against loss. | ### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Ensure it includes all required disclosures and that you understand your obligations and the landlord’s responsibilities. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 3. **Know the Notice Periods** – If you plan to move or if the landlord wants to change terms, be aware of the required notice periods. 4. **File a Complaint Early** – If the landlord fails to maintain habitability, file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office or local housing authority. 5. **Seek Legal Counsel** – For disputes over security deposits, eviction, or discrimination, consult a lawyer or a tenant advocacy group. ### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs**: [https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us](https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us) - **Texas Property Code (Chapter 24)**: [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PC/htm/PC.24.htm](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PC/htm/PC.24.htm) - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Search for “tenant rights Texas” in your city or county. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is intended for general informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Laws can change, and local ordinances may add additional protections. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
